title: When the Tide Falls
premise: Sable Dunmore, a ghostwriter who vanished from her hometown twenty years ago after a fire that killed her brother, is hired to write a rival author's memoir — only to discover the memoir is a thinly veiled account of that same fire, told from the other side. A lost letter postmarked eleven years ago surfaces in the manuscript, written by the rival's brother, the man Sable once loved and believed dead. As the coastal town's lantern festival approaches, Sable must confront the truth of who survived that night and at what cost, learning that the rival is not an enemy but a fellow survivor of the same silence. In the end, Sable chooses to publish the truth under her own name, reunites with Wren amid the festival tide, and finally claims the found family she abandoned rather than the safe, fragmentary life she built.
about_author: Cyrus Coldharbour is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who spent a decade writing other people's stories before daring to write one of their own. They live on a windswept Atlantic coast, where they collect tide charts and unanswered letters.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A meticulous ghostwriter takes a lucrative contract to write celebrity author Marisol Vane's memoir, telling herself the distance of the work will keep her safe. The emotional beat is wary professionalism masking old fear — Sable measures her life in small safe steps and intends to keep it that way.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. While transcribing Marisol's dictated chapters, Sable finds a physical letter tucked in the manuscript — postmarked eleven years ago, addressed to her, in handwriting she'd know anywhere: Wren's, the man who died in the harbor fire. The beat is vertigo; her careful present cracks open.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, with a flashback. Sable recalls the fire that killed her brother and supposedly Wren, and the twenty-year silence since. She begins reading the letter in stolen moments, learning Wren lived — and knew she thought him dead. The beat is grief colliding with betrayal.

chapters.title: The Rival's Version
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable and Marisol POVs. Sable realizes Marisol's memoir chapters describe the fire from the opposite shore of the harbor — and that Marisol is Wren's sister. A tense working dinner where neither woman says what both know. The beat is two people circling a shared wound.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable's found family — her landlady Odette and the bookshop regulars — notice her unraveling and offer the belonging she's never let herself accept. She drafts a letter to Wren and burns it. The beat is the comfort of half-measures, and their insufficiency.

chapters.title: The House on the Spit
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol confronts Sable, revealing she hired her deliberately: Wren is dying of an illness he's hidden, and Marisol wanted the memoir finished as a bridge back to Sable before time runs out. The beat is fury giving way to devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Tide
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable travels to the house on the spit and finds Wren alive, changed, unapologetic about his silence — he believed she chose to forget him. Their confrontation strips both bare. The beat is the raw honesty of two survivors naming the price they each paid.

chapters.title: Lending Pieces
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable and Wren POVs. They circle each other in the days before the lantern festival, offering fragments — a memory, a confession, a touch — while both withhold the whole heart. Marisol's memoir deadline forces Sable to choose what truth goes on the page. The beat is aching, almost-love.

chapters.title: The Festival of Lanterns
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, climax. At the festival, Sable publicly reads the final chapter of the memoir — the true account of the fire — under her own name for the first time in twenty years, surrendering her anonymity and her safety. Wren, frail but present, answers with the letter's missing last line. The beat is total risk.

chapters.title: When the Tide Falls
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, resolution. The tide goes out on the festival's last night, leaving the harbor floor walkable — the same tide that once separated them now carrying them across. Sable, Wren, Marisol, and Odette share a late supper as a chosen family; Sable signs her real name to the book. The beat is quiet, hard-won wholeness.
